records.summary: Emergency Assistance funds for rent, utilities and emergency shelter are provided for eligible low-income persons in order to help to maintain self-sufficiency and prevent homelessness. The purpose of Emergency Assistance is to avoid, eliminate or alleviate an emergency condition caused by an unforeseen circumstance resulting in a situation that calls for immediate action. To be eligible: an individual or family must be able to maintain after the crisis is alleviated; an individual or family must receive or be eligible for Cash Assistance (TANF, GA, SSI) or certain Medicaid programs; The emergency must have been the result of an unforeseen circumstance or a combination of circumstances that are beyond the recipients control. For questions regarding eligibility, email DHSS_DSSC@delaware.gov.

records.summary: The Refuge, a long-term, integrated sober-living facility located in Bear, Delaware. The Refuge provides separate housing units for men and women as well as women with children. These housing environments are supervised around the clock and provide residents support to achieve their sobriety and develop necessary skills to live safely and independently in the community. Structured clinical programs provide varying intensities of treatment to meet each resident's individual needs. Clinical staff include licensed master's level therapists, certified addiction counselors, peer support specialists, and a licensed practicing psychologist. While living at The Refuge, residents are afforded comprehensive medical and nursing care as well as psychiatric and medication-assisted treatment. As residents progress through the treatment continuum and their needs evolve, they are afforded opportunities for job placement, job skills training and ultimately, transition to sober-living homes, if needed.

records.organization: New Castle County Department of Community Services - Housing Authority - Housing Choice Vouchers
records.summary: Housing Choice Vouchers can be used either in public housing units that are operated and maintained by the Public Housing Authority or made available for low-income households to use toward rental assistance in the community. Eligibility includes those with disabilities and elderly persons whose income does not exceed 80% of the local median income. Voucher holders must locate their own unit. The voucher holder pays a portion of the rent each month and the voucher pays the remaining portion. The amount of assistance paid is determined by several factors including income, amount of rent being requested, utilities the renter is responsible for, and the size of the family. Housing Choice Vouchers are transferrable to other units including to another Public Housing Authority jurisdiction. Each Public Housing Authority (PHA) has their own application process and their own way of prioritizing their waitlist. Waitlists are often only open during certain times of the year and applications can only be accepted during those "open" times. It is essential for applicants on a waitlist to keep their contact information and current mailing address updated so they can respond when contacted by a PHA. The New Castle County Dept. of Community Services has a total of 1,825 Vouchers.

This program is funded through the Delaware Criminal Justice Council by the U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, Office for Victims of Crime, subgrant #VF14-1510.

records.summary: Breastfeeding is one of the most challenging and rewarding experiences a woman can have. It is a journey of emotional, personal and physical growth. It is the introduction into motherhood. But, breastfeeding can be very challenging. It can be scary, painful and overwhelming. Having a concrete support network is one of the strongest indicators of breastfeeding success. The Center utilizes a multi-dimensional method to support one in reaching their own personal breastfeeding goals.

records.summary: Junior Volunteer Program - Love animals and not sure if you can help? If you're 8-12 years of age, you can join our junior volunteer program! You and your chaperone or guardian (18 years+) just need to submit a volunteer application and attend a volunteer orientation to start helping cats and dogs in our care. You can socialize puppies and kittens, walk dogs together, help with grooming, and read to shelter pets. Once you reach 13 years of age, you can visit without supervision.
